meta.decision: Phase 198: tests/golden/wire_dict_baseline.json is preserved byte-unchanged. This file is the committed, reviewable expected-delta list the two datasheet-cited Fujitsu VPP corrections in tools/datasheet_overrides.json produce on top of it -- on the same terms as the 197 layer, the golden itself is never re-captured or re-baselined to make this phase's change disappear.
meta.honesty: This layer records only that these two records' vpp_mv wire value moved from the pre-198 decoded 12000 to 12500. It does not by itself establish that 12500 is electrically correct -- the figure was read visually from a datasheet page, not measured on a bench. Phase 198 also moved three electrical.vdd_mv values (FUJITSU/MBM27128, FUJITSU/MBM27C1001, FUJITSU/MBM27C4001, all 5500 -> 6000) and this measurement, run against the live capture, confirms none of those contributes a wire delta: vcc_mv and vdd_mv do not cross the wire, so the count here is 2, not 5.
meta.how_to_update: This layer is regenerated by the same script against the live database and never edited by hand. A new delta must name the chips and the reason in the commit message. Growing this list without a provenance justification is exactly the re-baselining the decision above exists to prevent -- see tests/test_wire_dict_equivalence.py's composition test for the anti-laundering assertions this fixture must satisfy.
meta.provenance: Both records are attributable to tools/datasheet_overrides.json entries: FUJITSU/MBM27C1001 (electrical.vpp_mv 12000 -> 12500, citing datasheets/MBM27C1001.pdf) and FUJITSU/MBM27C4001 (electrical.vpp_mv 12000 -> 12500, citing datasheets/MBM27C4001.pdf, the gh#66 community report's own attached datasheet). Generated programmatically from the live capture against the committed golden plus the 149, 153, 182, 194 and 197 delta layers -- never transcribed by hand, since the |<i> record-key suffix is a positional index within each manufacturer's list and would silently rot if any row is ever added or reordered.
